Surah 77: Al-Mursalat (The Emissaries). It is Meccan, except for verse 48, which is Medinan, and it has fifty verses.

﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾ ﴿and those that blow with vehement blowing﴾ ﴿and those that spread [things] widely﴾ ﴿and those that separate [truth from falsehood] decisively﴾ ﴿and those that deliver a reminder﴾. This is an oath by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by groups of angels whom He sent with His commands. They "blow with vehement blowing" in their passing, like the blowing of winds, hastening to carry out the command. [He swears] also by other groups who spread their wings in the air when descending with the revelation; or who spread the sharia (ash-shara'i') across the regions; or who revive dead souls with the knowledge of what they were revealed, so they separate between truth and falsehood, and thus they deliver a reminder to the prophets.

Surah 77: Al-Mursalat (The Emissaries). It is Meccan, except for verse 48, which is Medinan, and it has fifty verses.

﴿By those sent forth in succession﴾ ﴿and those that blow with vehement blowing﴾ ﴿and those that spread [things] widely﴾ ﴿and those that separate [truth from falsehood] decisively﴾ ﴿and those that deliver a reminder﴾. This is an oath by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by groups of angels whom He sent with His commands. They "blow with vehement blowing" in their passing, like the blowing of winds, hastening to carry out the command. [He swears] also by other groups who spread their wings in the air when descending with the revelation; or who spread the sharia (ash-shara'i') across the regions; or who revive dead souls with the knowledge of what they were revealed, so they separate between truth and falsehood, and thus they deliver a reminder to the prophets.

﴿Excuse﴾ for those who are right, ﴿or warning﴾ against those who are false. The placing of "spreading the laws" (*nashr al-shara'i'*), "spreading the souls" (*nashr al-nufus*) and "separating" (*al-farq*) before "casting" (*al-ilqa'*) may be intended to indicate that these are in fact the purpose of the casting and deserve to be given attention. Alternatively, it may be intended to indicate that each of the described attributes independently points to the groups so described deserving glorification and exaltation by the oath sworn by them. Had they been mentioned in the order in which they occur, it might have been understood that the combination of casting, spreading and separating is what necessitates the aforementioned deserving. Or the oath is by winds of punishment which He sent, so they blew strongly, and by winds of mercy which spread the clouds across the sky and so separated them, as in His saying, ﴿and makes it into fragments﴾. Or it is by clouds which spread out the dead [land] and so separated every kind of them from all the other kinds by shape, colour and all other properties. Or [it is by winds] which separated between those who thank God, exalted is He, and those who disbelieve in Him, and so cast the remembrance [of Him]. As for ﴿excuse﴾, it is for those who make excuse before God, exalted is He, through their repentance and seeking forgiveness for not having witnessed (p-78) the traces of His mercy, exalted is He, in the rain and giving thanks for it. As for ﴿warning﴾, it is for those who disbelieve in them and attribute them to the seasonal stars. The attribution of the casting of the remembrance to them is because they are a cause of its occurrence when the blessing in them is thanked for, or disbelieved in. Or it is an oath by the verses of the Qur'an sent down to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which abrogated (*naskh*, i.e. the cancelling of earlier rulings by later ones) all other scriptures, spread the traces of guidance from the eastern and western parts of the earth, separated between truth and falsehood, and so cast the remembrance of the truth into the corners of the worlds. As for ﴿al-'urf﴾, it is either the opposite of *al-nukr* (what is disapproved), and its being in the accusative is due to its being a reason (*'illa*), i.e. "We sent [them] for goodness and what is recognised as good", since the sending of angels of punishment is recognised as good by the prophets, peace be upon them, and the believers. Or it means "succession", from *'urf al-faras* (the mane of the horse, i.e. things following one another in a row), and its being in the accusative is as a circumstantial state (*hal*). And ﴿al-'udhr wa-l-nudhr﴾ are two verbal nouns: from *'adhara*, when it means "wiped away the wrongdoing", and from *andhara*, when it means "warned or frightened", and their being in the accusative is as substitutes (*badal*) for *dhikran*, or as reasons (*'illa*). They have also been read with the doubled consonant (*al-tathqil*).

Verse 7 of Surah al-Mursalat: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is surely going to occur.﴾ It is the answer to the oath: that is, what you are promised of the coming of the Resurrection will certainly take place, without doubt.
﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾ — effaced and annihilated, or their light is taken away.
And when the sky is split open (﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ فُرِجَتْ﴾). It is cleft and opened, so that it becomes gates.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 10:

﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾ They are made like grain that is winnowed with a winnowing shovel (minsaf) and the like, and the mountains are crumbled into dust (bussat al-jibal bassan). It is also said: they are uprooted from their places swiftly, from intasaftu al-shay' (I snatched the thing away) when I snatched it up quickly (ikhtataftuhu). It is also recited as (tummisat, "obliterated") and (furrijat, "split apart") and (nussifat, with the letter sin doubled, "blown away intensively").

It is their appointed time: the time was set for the messengers, at which they would appear to bear witness against their nations. That is at its arrival and its presence, since it is not fixed for them before it. Or they reached the appointed time they had been awaiting. It is also read (wuqqitat), in its original form, and with the lightened form in both cases.

For what Day were they postponed? (This is) a supplied phrase: a saying that serves as the answer to "when" (idha) in His words, "And when the Messengers are gathered to their appointed time." Or it is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the subject of "uqqitat," meaning: it is said, "For what Day were the matters concerning the Messengers postponed?" The purpose is to magnify that Day and to express wonder at its terror. And His, exalted be He, words:

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿For the Day of Decision﴾

This is an explanation (bayan) of "the Day of Postponement," and it is the day on which judgment is made between creation.

And what will make you know what the Day of Decision is?

"Ma" is the subject (mubtada') and "adraka" is its predicate (khabar), meaning: what has made you one who knows what it is? Thus "yawm al-fasl" (the Day of Decision) is placed in the position of the pronoun, for the sake of intensifying the terror and awe (tafzi' wa-tahwil), with "ma" being the predicate and "yawm al-fasl" the subject, not the reverse as preferred by Sibawayh. This is because the locus of the benefit is to explain that the Day of Decision is a matter that is unique and overwhelming, whose measure cannot be estimated and whose reality cannot be fully grasped; this is what the informative nature (khabariyyah) of "ma" conveys, not an explanation that the Day of Decision is some unique matter among matters, as the reverse would convey.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 15:

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾ That is: on that terrifying Day. "Woe" (waylun) is originally a verbal noun in the accusative, standing in place of its verb, but it has been shifted to the nominative, to indicate the permanence and continuity of destruction for the one against whom it is invoked. "On that Day" (yawma'idhin) is its adverbial complement (zarf) or its qualifier (sifah).

Qur'an 77:16, "Did We not destroy the former peoples?" (﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples?﴾), like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud, because of their denial of it. It is also recited (qurria) as (nahlak) with a fatha on the nun, from (halakahu), with the same meaning as (ahlakahu), "He destroyed him."

ﷺ-free passage; translating faithfully.

﴿Then We shall make the later ones follow them.﴾ With the nominative reading (ﺮَﻓْﻊ, "raf'"), on the basis of "then": "We shall make the later ones follow them," that is, their counterparts who travel the same path in disbelief and denial. This is a threat to the disbelievers of Makkah. It is also read as "Then We shall make them follow" (thumma sa-nutbi'uhum), and read in the jussive (nutbi'hum), coordinated with "nuhlik" (We destroy). In that case, "the later ones" means those who came after the ones mentioned in destruction, such as the people of Lut, Shu'ayb, and Musa, upon them be peace.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 18:

﴿Thus﴾: like that heinous deed.

﴿We do with the criminals﴾: that is, Our practice (sunnah) continues in accordance with that.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 19:

﴿Woe on that Day﴾ i.e., the day when We destroyed them.

﴿to the deniers﴾ of the signs of God Most High and His prophets. There is no repetition in it, because the first woe (wayl) is for the punishment of the Hereafter, and this one is for the punishment of this world.

﴿Did We not create you﴾ That is: did We not decree you?

﴿from a base fluid﴾ That is: from a filthy, base drop of semen (nutfah).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 21:

﴿Then We placed him in a firm lodging﴾ — that is, the womb.
﴿Ila qadarin ma'lum﴾ (up to a known measure): up to a known measure of time, which God, exalted is He, determined for birth to be nine months, or less than that, or more.

﴿فَقَدَرْنا﴾, i.e., *fa-qaddarnāhu* (so We determined it). It has also been read with a doubled *dal* (shaddah), *فَقَدَّرْنا*. Alternatively, the phrase may be read as *﴿فَقَدَرْنا عَلى ذَلِكَ﴾* (So We determined upon that), on the basis that *qadr* (determination) refers to what accompanies the actual existence of the thing determined.

﴿فَنِعْمَ القادِرُونَ﴾ i.e., "How excellent are the Determiners!" (*naḥnu*), meaning We Ourselves.
(p-80) ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ by Our power over that, or over the return.

﴿Did We not make the earth a receptacle,﴾ "Al-kifat" is the name of that which is gathered and drawn together, from kafata al-shay' (to gather and draw something together): when one gathers and binds it, like al-dimam and al-jima' for that which is gathered and collected. That is, "Did We not make it a receptacle that gathers (the living and the dead)?"

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 26:

﴿Living﴾ in great number upon its surface.

﴿And dead﴾, not confined within its belly. It has also been said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) described by it for the sake of emphasis (mubalaghah). It has also been said that it is the plural of "kafit," like "sa'im" and "siyam," or of "kift," meaning a receptacle, applied to the earth in consideration of its places (biqa'). It has also been said that the indefiniteness of "living and dead" is because the living and dead of mankind are only part of the living and the dead. It has also been said that their accusative case is in the sense of a circumstantial state (hal) from an omitted word, meaning: a receptacle (kifatan) that gathers you, living and dead.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 27:

﴿And We placed in it firm mountains﴾ i.e., mountains that are fixed (thawabit).

﴿Lofty (shamikhat)﴾: tall, towering peaks. The description of a masculine plural by a feminine plural is regular (mutt-arid) for non-rational beings, as in dajin and dawajin (domestic animal, pl.).

﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water (furat)﴾: by creating in it rivers and springs.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 28:

﴿Woe on that Day to those who deny﴾ these great bounties of the like kind.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 29:

﴿Proceed﴾, i.e., it will be said to them on that day, for rebuke and reproach: "Proceed."

﴿To that which you used to deny﴾ in the world, of the punishment.

**"Depart"** (intensive, addressed to them specifically).

**"To a shadow"**, i.e., the shadow of the smoke of Hellfire, like His saying: ﴿and a shadow of black smoke﴾. It is also read as (انْطَلَقُوا) in the past tense, a report after the command of their acting in accordance with its requirement, since they are compelled to it, willingly or unwillingly.

**"Having three branches"**: it branches, because of its magnitude, into three branches, as is the nature of a great smoke; you see it separating into tufts. It was also said: a tongue of fire emerges and encompasses the disbelievers like a pavilion, and three branches split off from its smoke, shading them until He finishes their reckoning, while the believers are in the shade of the Throne. It was said: the specificity of the number three is either because the barriers of the self from the lights of holiness are the senses, the imagination and the estimative faculty (al-wahm), or because what leads to this punishment is the satanic estimative faculty located in the brain, the wrathful beastly faculty to the right of the heart, and the appetitive animal faculty to its left. For this reason it was said: one branch stands above the disbeliever, one branch to his right, and one branch to his left.

(p-81) ﴿Neither cooling shade﴾ is said to mock them, and it was included because of what the word "shade" (ẓill) might suggest. ﴿Nor does it spare them from the blaze﴾ means: it does not spare them from the heat of the blaze at all.

﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a castle﴾. That is, every spark is like one of the castles in its enormity. It was also said: it refers to the thick trunks of trees; the singular is "qaṣrah," like jamr and jamrah (ember and ember-piece). It was read as (kal-qaṣar) with two fatḥahs, and this means the necks of camels, or the necks of palm trees, like shajarah and shajar (tree and trees). It was read as (kal-quṣur), meaning the plural of qaṣr (castles), like rahn and ruhun (pledge and pledges). And it was read as (kal-qaṣr), the plural of qaṣrah.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 33:

﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾ It is said: it is the plural of "jamal" (camel), and the ta' is for the feminine form of the plural. It is said: jamal, plural jimal, and also jimalah (jimmalah). It is also said: it is a collective noun (ism jam'), like hijarah (stones). ﴿Yellow﴾: for a spark, because of the fiery nature it contains, is yellowish. It is also said: black, because the blackness of camels inclines toward yellow. The first (interpretation) is a comparison in size; this one is a comparison in colour, in number, in succession, in intermingling, and in movement. It is also recited as (jimalatun), the plural of jimmalah, and it has been recited with it, meaning a great rope from the cables of ships and the hawsers of bridges. The comparison lies in its length and in its coiling.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 34:

﴿Woe on that day to the deniers.﴾

This is a reference to their entry into the Fire: "This is a day in which they will not speak," meaning a day on which they will not speak anything, because questioning, answering and reckoning had already ended before that. The Day of Resurrection is long, with stations (mawatin) and times (mawaqit): they speak at one time and not at another, so each time is expressed by "day." Or the meaning is that they will not speak anything that benefits them, for that counts as a kind of speech. It is also read with the word "day" in the accusative (nasb), meaning: what has been detailed occurs on a day when they will not speak.

Surah 77, verse 36, in Abu al-Su'ud's commentary (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim):

﴿And it will not be permitted for them, so they will not make excuses.﴾ It is a conjunction (ʿaṭf) on "yuʾdhanu" (it is permitted), falling within the scope of the negation; that is, there will not be for them a permission, and an excuse following it, without the excuse being made a consequence (musabbab) of the permission, as would be the case if it were put in the accusative (naṣb).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verses 37–38:

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾ between the truth and falsehood, and between the one who is in the right and the one who is in the wrong.

﴿We have gathered you﴾ is an address to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And the former ones﴾ from the nations. This is an affirmation and clarification of the Decision (al-fasl).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verses 37–38:

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ ﴿This is the Day of Decision﴾ between the truth and falsehood, and between the one who is in the right and the one who is in the wrong.

﴿We have gathered you﴾ is an address to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And the former ones﴾ from the nations. This is an affirmation and clarification of the Decision (al-fasl).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 39:

(p-82) ﴿So if you have any scheme, then scheme against Me!﴾ For all those whom you used to follow and imitate are present here. This is a rebuke to them for their scheming against the believers in the world, and a demonstration of their impotence.
﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾. This is because it became clear that they have no stratagem for escaping the punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, the God-conscious﴾ from disbelief and denial.

﴿Are amid shade and springs﴾
And fruits of whatever they desire. That is: they will be settled in every kind of luxury and every form of enjoyment.

﴿Eat and drink with ease for what you used to do﴾ is governed by an implied verb of saying, and it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun of "the God-conscious" (al-muttaqūn) in the predicate; that is, "being told: Eat and drink with ease for what you used to do in this world of righteous deeds."

Qur'an 77:44: "Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers."

"Indeed, thus" (kadhalika): the great reward.

"We reward the good-doers" (najzi al-muhsinin): that is, in their beliefs and their deeds, not a lesser reward than this.
Woe on that Day to the deniers. (Commentary:) Since their enemies attained this abundant reward, while they themselves remained in the lasting and severe punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 46:

﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals.﴾ It is supplied with a saying which is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to "the deniers," meaning: woe is established for them, being said to them thus, as a reminder to them of their state in the world, and of what they brought upon themselves through preferring the fleeting enjoyment that soon passes over the everlasting bliss. He gave the reason for this by their being criminals, indicating that every criminal's end is this. It has also been said: it is an independent statement addressed to the deniers in the world after the explanation of the outcome of their state, and this was confirmed by the words of the Exalted:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 47:

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ (this is said) for the increase of rebuke and reproach.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 48:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down,"⁠﴾ i.e., obey Allah, humble yourselves before Him, submit to accepting His revelation and following His religion, and abandon this arrogance and haughtiness.

﴿They do not bow down.⁠﴾ They do not humble themselves, they do not accept that, and they persist in the arrogance they are upon. It is also said: when they are commanded to pray, or to bow (ruku'), they do not do it. It was narrated that it was revealed when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the Thaqif to pray, and they said, "We will not do it, for it would be a disgrace upon us." The Prophet (ﷺ), upon him be blessings and peace, said: "There is no good in a religion that has no bowing (ruku') and no prostration (sujud)." It is also said: it refers to the Day of Resurrection, when they are called to prostrate and are unable to do so.

Woe on that Day to the deniers. ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾

And in it there is an indication that the disbelievers are addressed with the subsidiary (furu') rulings with respect to being held accountable.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 77, verse 50:

﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ That is: after the Qur'an, which speaks with the reports of the two abodes (this world and the Hereafter) and the accounts of the two creations (the first and the second), in a wondrous, inimitable style, founded upon decisive proofs and manifest demonstrations.

﴿will they believe﴾ if they do not believe in it. It is also read as (tu'minun) in the second person (ikhitab), i.e., "will you believe."

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Whoever recites Surat al-Mursalat, it is written for him that he is not among the polytheists.﴾
